label: NIST controlled blocking
summary: NIST describes blocking as holding nuisance factors constant inside homogeneous blocks while varying the factor of interest.

label: NIST balanced blocking criterion
summary: NIST defines a blocking factor by equal occurrence of each primary-factor level at each nuisance-factor level.

label: NIST residual nuisance randomization
summary: NIST recommends blocking important nuisance variables and randomizing to reduce contamination by remaining nuisance variables.

label: NIST hypothetical blocked wafer allocation
summary: NIST illustrates a hypothetical design putting four wafers with different dosages in each of three furnace runs.

label: Nosek preregistration definition
summary: Nosek et al. (2018) define analysis preregistration as committing to analytic steps without prior knowledge of outcomes.

label: Nosek postdiction diagnosticity warning
summary: Nosek et al. warn that postdictive NHST analyses may yield p-values of unknown diagnosticity.

label: Nosek 2018 preregistration evidence limit
summary: Nosek et al. (2018) report theoretical and correlational support for preregistration but insufficient experimental evidence of a reproducibility advantage.

label: Nosek preexisting-data blinding
summary: Nosek et al. explain that tests of predictions using preexisting data depend on blinded analysis decisions, which face risks when data have already been observed.

label: Nosek biased preregistered decision trees
summary: Nosek et al. warn that preregistered decision trees can still embed bias, such as stopping after achieving p < 0.05.

label: Nosek complete reporting across studies
summary: Nosek et al. argue that reporting all planned outcomes matters because preregistration alone cannot eliminate multiple-comparison and selective-reporting problems.

label: Nosek Registered Reports workflow
summary: Nosek et al. describe Registered Reports as pre-outcome methodological peer review with in-principle acceptance, followed by review of execution and adherence.

label: Nosek exploratory-to-holdout testing
summary: Nosek et al. describe splitting a dataset, sealing the holdout and preregistering exploration-derived predictions before unsealing it.
